A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RL-MILP solver. Their complete text, equations, figures, and tables support comparison, including v3 Appendices A–E. v1 has no appendices, and material moved into v3's appendices can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 Section 4 and Tables 2–3 report original experiments comparing solvers and ablating architectural components on generated MILP instances.

after.justification: v3 Section 4 and Tables 1–3 report original solver comparisons, reward-bias and neighborhood experiments, and architectural ablations.

M1.justification: v3 substantially replaces both phases' rewards with violation-based and objective-dependent terms controlled by β. Transformer/Critic inputs change from objt to objr and objb, training gains a phase1 warm-up, and phase2 search accepts only feasible, nonworsening moves. These change training and inference procedures, beyond the added pseudocode.

E1.justification: v3 adds D50×20 and D300×100 alongside the retained D9×18 and D100×50 datasets. These extend the tested problem-size regimes, while retaining the same synthetic generation family and optimization task with exclusively integer variables.

E2.justification: v1 Table 2 compares against Gurobi, M_MLP, and M_CNN. v3 Table 1 retains these comparators and adds classic local search, initialized with the RL agent's first feasible solution to compare subsequent search performance.

E3.justification: Main comparisons retain a 100-second limit, but v3 includes a 600-second Gurobi reference when defining the best-known objective and introduces #win. D9×18 training increases from 500 to 5,000 updates. Added experiments vary β and action magnitudes; the neighborhood study uses 300 seconds and 10,000 updates.

E4.justification: v3 adds reward-bias sensitivity experiments and a neighborhood-size study testing movement magnitudes. Table 3 also replaces v1's eight PE/PT/SL combinations with a revised selection that additionally removes the Transformer and MPNN separately, testing their respective contributions to solution quality and feasibility.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-training-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both use 100 test instances per dataset; the added result rows do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Results are substantially replaced and expanded. On D100×50, v1 Table 2 reports a 1.33% gap for the proposed solver; v3 Table 1 reports 0.55%, 0.38%, and 0.34% for β = 1, 0.6, and 0.3. M_CNN feasibility changes from 100% to 0% across those later settings. These accompany method and protocol changes, so they are not same-setting performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: v3 adds Proposition 1 and Appendix A's formal feasible-set proof of objr ≤ objopt ≤ obj′ < objb, extending the interval argument used informally in v1. It also corrects the equilibration-scaling justification from a nonnegative to a positive multiplier. The theoretical addition does not establish convergence or optimality of the solver.

C1.justification: The core claims about generating complete solutions through RL and using a Transformer-based GNN remain. v3 adds theoretically grounded learning and search strategies to the explicit contributions and strengthens the larger-dataset accuracy claim from roughly a 1% gap to below 1%.

C2.justification: v3 introduces substantial interpretations of reward bias, neighborhood size, and the different feasibility/quality roles of MPNN and Transformer components. It removes v1's detailed ablation-specific explanations of critic spikes and phase-layer failures, along with the conclusion's continuous-variable extension discussion. Integer-only evaluation and the lack of optimality guarantees remain acknowledged elsewhere.

D1.justification: Appendices C and E add training pseudocode, hardware and software versions, RMSprop hyperparameters, 64-instance concurrent training, component depths, and implementation-source links. These substantially expand reproducibility information. The generation parameters in v3 Table 4 were already supplied in v1 Table 1.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations supporting rounding, LP theory, local search, and neural optimization, including Cont and Heidari, Shaw, and Son et al., while removing the Zhang et al. 2023 survey. The related-work taxonomy remains, while the novelty statement becomes more specifically framed around full end-to-end RL for integer MILP.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, methodology, and results discussion are extensively rewritten. v3 introduces nested background/method subsections and explicit research questions, shortens the conclusion, and redistributes reward explanations, search pseudocode, and generation details into appendices. This is substantial narrative reorganization beyond renumbering.

P2.justification: v3 restructures the main results into a wide table with dataset columns and β groups, redesigns the ablation table, and adds a neighborhood-results table. The architecture figure changes its inputs, the reward diagram is revised and moved to Appendix B, and a new two-panel reward plot is added. Headers, typography, and appendix layouts also change.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses important gaps in v1's validation: local search supplies a direct search control, while bias, neighborhood, and MPNN/Transformer studies test specific design choices. Appendices C and E substantially improve training transparency and reproducibility information. These gains outweigh the loss of some earlier ablation discussion, although evaluation remains confined to synthetic integer MILPs and lacks run-level uncertainty reporting.
